narrative.overview: The interface is a drafting table set beside a lit model. The model, a terraced voxel island in cool daylight, is the subject; the controls are the blueprint paper around it: deep navy ink, hairline pale-blue rules, small precise type. Cyan marks what you can touch. Amber marks what has been measured.
keyCharacteristics: Navy ink glass over a bright diorama; the scene is never hidden behind chrome.
Two voices of color: cyan for interaction, amber for values.
Hairline rules instead of heavy borders or shadows.
Share Tech for headings only; Roboto for reading; monospace for numbers.
Everything explains itself on hover, in plain sentences.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Cyan is for things you can act on; amber is for things that are measured. Never swap them, never add a third accent to the UI.

rules.name: The City Glows Rule
rules.body: UI color stays cold and muted so the lit city carries the saturation.

rules.name: The Short Stencil Rule
rules.body: Share Tech is for short headings only; never set a sentence in it.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px Rule color at 10 to 25% opacity. Never thicker, never opaque.

dos: Do keep cyan for controls and amber for values (The Two Voices Rule).
Do give every control a one or two sentence hover explanation in plain American English.
Do use the kit in site/src/world/ui/kit.tsx before writing a new control; extend it rather than restyling in place.
Do keep panels translucent and dimming so the scene shows through.
Do fix the decimals of every shown number.
donts: Don't add a second UI accent; amber, pink and lime are for data only.
Don't use solid opaque panels, heavy borders or hard shadows.
Don't animate layout size; slide, fade or recolor instead, 150 to 300 ms.
Don't set long text in Share Tech.
Don't design for phone widths in /world.
Don't use em dashes in interface descriptions.
